text:
alyssa (support): FYI customer Paul from acme-corp reports all tenant charts empty in Console after they flipped the new sidecar proxy in their VPC. Graphs show "no data" but API calls succeed. Can someone triage? @eng-runtime @networking :thinking:

jordan (sre): Which metrics specifically? traces or token usage? any error spike in API?

alyssa (support): Token usage + embeddings per-tenant in the last 24h. The raw API call logs (from their onprem gateway) show 200 responses. Example request we received forwarded to us:

```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-private.example
X-Tenant: acme-prod
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
```

But in our ingress logs the request arrives missing X-Tenant: header. Logs show: `headers: { authorization: ***, x-tenant: "" }`

maya (eng-runtime): That suggests header strip or rewrite happening in the customer sidecar/proxy path. If tenant header is empty we won't attribute metrics to the tenant (falls into untagged ingestion). Is customer using our auth-proxy sidecar or a third-party envoy?

paul (acme-corp): We rolled out a custom Envoy filter to normalize headers for other services. We did not touch Redwood-specific headers intentionally.

samir (networking): Can you paste the envoy filter snippet? Common mistake: :replace_headers or header normalization that lowercases/cleans unknown headers. Also path-based routing can drop HEADER_PREFIX_* variables.

paul (acme-corp): Snippet:
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
    request_rules:
      - header: ".*"
        on_header_present:
          metadata_namespace: envoy.lb
          key: whatever
```

jordan (sre): That wildcard rule looks suspicious. It may be matching X-Tenant and clearing it when converting to metadata. Also confirm whether there's any header_rewrite in upstream cluster config.

alyssa (support): Repro steps I ran from my laptop to customer's private endpoint (they gave a jumpbox):
1) curl -v -H "X-Tenant: acme-prod" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://private-api.acme.internal/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
2) On jumpbox tcpdump on 127.0.0.1: `sudo tcpdump -A -s 0 port 443`
3) Observe TLS decrypted by sidecar (they did TLS termination) and request after sidecar to Redwood shows missing X-Tenant

Sample extracted header line from their sidecar egress log: `request.headers["x-tenant"] = ""`

maya (eng-runtime): If header is empty when we ingest, our metrics pipeline will bucket into an unknown-tenant shard and isn't shown in per-tenant dashboards. Two possible causes: 1) header being rewritten to empty by envoy filter; 2) header moved into metadata and removed from outgoing headers (we expect it in plaintext for attribution).

samir (networking): Can we get the sidecar config or Envoy admin config dump? Also need the raw request capture between their sidecar and our private gateway.

paul (acme-corp): Uploading envoy config now, link: https://acme-files/reports/envoy_dump_2026-03-12.json (private).

ops-bot: New file uploaded by paul: envoy_dump_2026-03-12.json :page_facing_up:

jordan (sre): I glanced at the dump: header_to_metadata rule indeed matches `x-tenant` and sets metadata then removes header (that filter is configured with `remove_header: true`). That explains disappearance.

maya (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation: we can accept tenant identity from metadata if present — but that requires a tiny patch to the private ingress to check both headers and metadata when attributing metrics. I can prepare a quick patch to runtime to fallback to metadata.x-tenant.

alyssa (support): Is that low-risk? Customer wants dashboards restored ASAP.

maya (eng-runtime): Yes low-risk. Add unit test + one canary node in their Private cluster. Rollout sequence: patch runtime -> canary -> verify tenant metrics flow -> widen. I estimate ~2 hours including CI.

jordan (sre): Meanwhile, for immediate customer relief they can flip the envoy filter to set `remove_header: false` or stop the header_to_metadata rule. That requires their change and redeploy. Paul, can you do that quickly?

paul (acme-corp): I can disable the filter and redeploy right now. ETA 20m. Will post after redeploy.

alyssa (support): Thanks. If they can't redeploy quickly, Maya's patch is backup. Also will open a ticket for a backfill: any metrics that arrived without tenant will need reprocessing if we can match by request_id. We should record which ingestors saw untagged events and capture raw envelopes.

maya (eng-runtime): Action items:
- I will open PR to accept metadata fallback and run a canary (PR #1428)
- Jordan: collect list of untagged ingestion shards since 03/11 (for backfill)
- Alyssa: coordinate with Paul and update customer slack/channel

jordan (sre): Collected shard list and sample envelopes (linked in internal bucket). There's ~12k envelopes for tenant `acme-prod` that lost X-Tenant. We can re-ingest if we have mapping via request_id.

paul (acme-corp): Redeploy done. Verified header appears in our egress logs again: `x-tenant: acme-prod`. Checking Console now... dashboards still empty, give me a minute to flush caches?

alyssa (support): I see a small spike now for acme-prod token usage in the raw logs. Console still showing "no data" for per-tenant charts — could be caching/aggregation delay (~5-10m).

ops-bot: Deploy for acme sidecar completed :white_check_mark:

paul (acme-corp): Console updated! Charts greying back in. Many thanks.

maya (eng-runtime): I'll keep the PR ready in case others have similar filters. Also adding detection in onboarding docs: warn about header_to_metadata with remove_header=true for any tenant headers.

alyssa (support): I'll close the support ticket after confirming with Paul tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :tada:

paul (acme-corp): Thanks all, appreciate the quick help. :pray:
